response.answer: For production acceptance, DeepLab and U-Net are strong baselines. DeepLab excels in semantic segmentation, while U-Net is favored for medical image segmentation. LFT-UNet combines U-Net with Transformer for lightweight segmentation.

results.title: LFT-UNet: A lightweight fusion of transformer and U-Net architectures for embedded medical image segmentation - ScienceDirect
results.content: # LFT-UNet: A lightweight fusion of transformer and U-Net architectures for embedded medical image segmentation. Due to the outstanding performance of the U-Net architecture in medical image segmentation, numerous researchers have proposed various improvements based on U-Net. For example, Attention U-Net [2] introduced an Attention Gate module to enhance focus on local regions. U-Net Transformer(UNETR) [8] replaced the Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs)-based encoder with Transformer structures, achieving excellent performance in three-dimensional (3D) medical image segmentation. With the increasing adoption of Transformer models in medical image segmentation, many networks have heavily incorporated Transformer modules to capture global information from feature maps, resulting in a rapid increase in the parameter count. Therefore, when designing a versatile medical image segmentation network, it is essential to reconsider the choice of the base U-Net model with practical application in mind, including potential deployment on embedded platforms. After thorough analysis and exploration of U-Net and its variants, a re-engineered medical image segmentation network, named LFT-UNet, has been proposed.
